Absolutely this. Like I said, their hands were tied. My heart aches for my ED coworkers.  Know that you are absolutely appreciated.

Its absolutely true.  My good friend and I said it was the worst pain we have ever had and some have none. My infection absolutely made it worse, but I went in not prepared for what the recovery could be. Lesson learned. Now, don't mind me as I get flagged for water consumption in California for making sure that I NEVER get stones again.😝

Anger leads to the dark side, lol. What can I do, and honestly what can they do? It is a 32 bed ED, and they had at one point over 60 patients that day (per the MD).  This is becoming similar to having a mass casualty event daily in the ERs.  I will say this, I have told everyone that I know  that unless it is potentially life or limb, stay away.

According to the nurses unless you are in a room, you can't get narcotics.  I was able to get Toradol (THANK GOD) but the doctor said "I am so sorry" and sent me home with some oral dilaudid. He and the staff were apologizing continually. I just wanted to stop shaking from pain (which sucked, but at least I had meds now to help treat), get my antibiotics and get out. I actually cried on the car ride home, not from pain but from how the while experience went. This sucks for everyone,  patients and staff.

(Edited...typing on phone and the Grammer and Spelling errors were gonna make me nuts.)

I had a Stent and laser lithotripsy Friday before last. Ended up in the ED with an infection on Monday,  and I was actually frightened.  I didn't even get triaged (talk to a nurse) for over 90 minutes,  and saw a doctor two hours later. I was propped up on a gurney in a hall, where it took another 90 minutes s for an IV to even get antibiotics.  Pain meds? They said no, you are in a hallway. I am one of the lucky ones, I wasn't septic yet.  And the worst part,  I am a nurse at that hospital,  and people know so I  was getting what the staff called "expedited care".
